summary: Rabbi Tawil discusses the importance of maintaining a growth mindset by surrounding oneself with people of higher capability, rather than settling for comfort. He uses the Mishna in Pirkei Abot regarding being the tail of the lion to illustrate why one should always seek to challenge themselves in Torah and life.
questions: Why is it better to be the tail of the lion than the head of the jackals?
How can we avoid becoming stagnant in our spiritual growth?
Why do we sometimes resist challenging ourselves?
How does our environment affect our ability to grow?
